answers.answer: UNKNOWN as a consistent prediction: the article contradicts itself. Its t=50 example and later accepted-use rule say A can use at t=60 if nothing else intervenes and the refused t=5 attempt starts neither wait. But the earlier t=5 bullet says both waits restart, which would move A’s personal expiry to t=65 and even conflict with the next t=10 bullet. I cannot establish which rule to trust from this article alone.
quote: At 5 seconds, A tries again. The attempt is refused and both waits start again from that moment.
At 10 seconds, another viewer could use it. A still has to wait until 60 seconds.
If viewer B uses it at 50 seconds, B starts a new shared wait. A’s personal wait and that shared wait both end at 60 seconds, so A can use it then if nothing else intervenes.

Each accepted use starts fresh waits. If someone else uses it at 55 seconds instead, A’s own minute still ends at 60, but chat’s shared wait lasts until 65.
Here, “accepted” means the use passed the access and cooldown checks; a later action can still fail. A refusal for access or cooldown starts neither wait.

answers.answer: The Artist badge alone does not satisfy Artists, so the command does not run and the viewer receives the permission refusal. The bot also attempts to speak that refusal even with Read it aloud off. Actual audio depends on TTS setup, settings and playback; positive Minimum bits blocks the zero-bit refusal, approval can hold it, and the per-viewer denial-speech throttle can prevent a new attempt.
quote: An Artist badge alone does not pass an Artists command requirement. The person needs Artist standing recorded in the bot or a higher qualifying role.

The command does not run. By default, the bot replies in chat in the channel’s one bot voice: “You don’t have permission to use that command.”
It also attempts to speak that line in the channel’s bot voice, even when the command’s Read it aloud switch is off.

You do not need text to speech to set access or cooldowns. To hear a refusal, the channel’s TTS setup, settings and playback must allow it.
A positive Minimum bits setting blocks this speech because the refusal carries 0 bits.
The bot attempts denial speech at most once every 30 seconds for each viewer in a channel, shared across all denied commands.
